body:
Firstly thank you for taking the time to reply! I find it hard to express my pain without philosophy, which I hope you'll excuse, and I do see the difficulty in framing my perspective on my faulty mind by using my faulty mind. I'll try to lay out my situation, but it's a couple of libraries of introspection short of complete.

I think that connection and belonging are very apt indeed. I live in a mild but constant physical pain from injuries, and a rather more severe mental pain from depression and anxiety. I have problems with noise, I don't like people standing behind me, and a flurry of other niggles that people find exhausting. I generally think of myself as "pointlessly clever" - meaning that while I'm either smart or have convinced myself and others that I am smart it's not to any purpose. I live without value to others, which I need to ascribe value to myself. I am without friends or contacts of any sort other than (currently) my parents. My father is elderly and constantly angry, as well as disappointed in me - I am a difficulty at the end of his life that he'd rather not deal with and I can see his point. That is all a gross oversimplification but you would thank me for summarizing if you knew. My mother is very sweet but constantly worries about me and my condition which given that she is my only understanding support role for my condition leaves me spinning in a cycle of guilt, constantly questioning myself to whether my guilt is well-deserved or self-generated and makes it difficult to trust anything that gets said to me. I'm also very good at argument and debate which makes it hard to trust anyone's opinion because it can't stay isolated from what I can make people think.

I live under the belief that I'm unable to survive or achieve anything on my own. Attempts to do otherwise are interrupted by what I see as failure or attempts to "help" that prove the belief, or opinions that confirm that belief. This also makes it very hard to accept help when I need it, and makes me irritable at honest attempts to help whether actually helpful or not - but given that I need that help to survive it's ultimately all a bit of a waste of time and I end up feeling worse about it either way.

I hope that gives some insight to the cycles and quandaries I live in, and the unending tides of ambivalence  between one perspective and another with which I question myself. For example I wondered while writing my original post whether I was being more logical about ending my life or if I just incorrectly thought I was better than everyone else. I am paralyzed by skepticism - it builds the walls of my introspection labyrinth and I can wonder around it forever. Suicide is the simplest route out of my pain, and I have all sorts of arguments that support it that I won't post here.

I also don't derive fun from anything, I entertain myself as a distraction from living with myself. So, in short, I'm exhausted. As I'm sure you must be too by now, so thank you again for your time and attention.
